questions.question: In an $n\times n$ matrix, which entries lie on the main diagonal?
options: The entries $a_{ij}$ with $i\ne j$.
The entries $a_{ii}$, same row and column
Only the entries in the last column.
Only the first row entries.

questions.question: Which direction does the main diagonal run?
options: Along the last column only.
From the upper-right corner to the lower-left corner.
Along the first row only.
From the upper-left corner to the lower-right corner.

questions.question: Why is the main diagonal central to the identity matrix?
options: The identity matrix is defined by its anti-diagonal entries.
The identity matrix has arbitrary main diagonal entries.
The identity matrix has zeros on the main diagonal and ones elsewhere.
The identity matrix has ones on the main diagonal and zeros elsewhere.

questions.question: What does the trace of a square matrix add together?
options: All off-diagonal entries.
All entries of the matrix.
The main diagonal entries.
The entries in the first column.

questions.question: For a square matrix, what is the relationship between the main diagonal and the off-diagonal entries?
options: They are the same entries written in reverse order.
Every entry is both diagonal and off-diagonal.
Off-diagonal entries are those not on the main diagonal
The main diagonal consists only of zero entries.

questions.question: In $\begin{pmatrix}1&2\\3&4\end{pmatrix}$, what are the main diagonal entries?
In $\begin{pmatrix}2&5&7\\0&-1&4\\3&8&6\end{pmatrix}$, which list is the main diagonal?
What are the main diagonal entries of $I_3$?
For a $4\times4$ matrix $A$, which entry is on the main diagonal?
In a $5\times5$ matrix, how many entries are on the main diagonal?
Why is the main diagonal defined here for square matrices?
options: Non-square matrices have no entries with equal indices.
The notation $a_{ii}$ matches row and column indices
Only square matrices can contain zero entries.
The determinant of every rectangular matrix is one.

questions.question: Which statement links the main diagonal to diagonal matrices?
options: A diagonal matrix ignores the main diagonal.
A diagonal matrix must have zero entries on the main diagonal.
A diagonal matrix may have nonzero entries only on the main diagonal.
A diagonal matrix is determined by its last row.

questions.question: What is the difference between the main diagonal and the anti-diagonal?
options: They are always the same set of entries.
Main diagonal: top-left to bottom-right; anti-diagonal: opposite
The anti-diagonal contains only zero entries.
The main diagonal exists only for identity matrices.

questions.question: For $A=\begin{pmatrix}4&0&1\\2&5&3\\7&8&-2\end{pmatrix}$, what is the sum of the main diagonal entries?
Which entry of a $3\times3$ matrix is both on the main diagonal and in the second row?
A $3\times3$ matrix has main diagonal entries $2$, $0$, and $-5$. What is the trace?
Why can two matrices with the same main diagonal still be very different?
options: The main diagonal determines every entry.
The trace records all entries individually.
Their off-diagonal entries may differ.
Equal diagonal entries force equal determinants.

questions.question: What information does the main diagonal give for trace but not for determinant in general?
options: It directly gives the trace by summing its entries.
It directly gives every determinant by summing its entries.
It directly gives all row operations.
It directly gives the inverse of every matrix.
